dossier.public_summary: The 5-day dip is locked to the star’s own 5.19-day spot cycle with huge 1.7–6.7% variability, shows a strong 230-ppm secondary eclipse at phase 0.56 and large phase-curve swing, deep grazing-like transits and depth changes from sector to sector. Together this matches a stellar companion/eclipsing binary on the target, not a 2 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Secondary dip well above noise and far above brightenings, with depth ~38% of primary, consistent with stellar eclipse not planetary occultation. Hot giant could show tiny secondary, not this deep.
Large out-of-transit swing outside the dip comparable to transit depth, indicating ellipsoidal/spot modulation from a close binary rather than a planet.
Dip period identical to stellar rotation (17247–67075 ppm variability) with huge spot amplitude, not expected for a 5.08d planet.
Depths inconsistent and dominated by a few outliers including negative/zero transits, inconsistent with stable planetary transits.
